note: CEILINGS, not a measured baseline. These are budgets a healthy run must stay under, with 3-6x headroom over observed healthy numbers so machine drift, a cold runner or a noisy neighbor does not fire them - and so they never need re-blessing per machine. Breaching one means an order-of-magnitude regression, not jitter. HEADROOM IS NOT UNIFORM: ceilings are keyed on interaction, not deck, so the same cap covers a 7.4ms and a 16.0ms healthy TOTAL. Thin end is gallery TOTAL (~3x); wide end means a 5x regression on a cheap deck stays green. See engineering/decisions/2026-08-03-performance-guard.md.

observed.note: RANGES across THREE independent runs of the same suite on the same machine (2026-08-03, headless Chromium, 4x CPU throttle, 40-slide decks), not one run's numbers - because one run's numbers do not reproduce. Context only; nothing compares against these. navigation renderP50 is BIMODAL: the whole-deck memo hits read ~0.0ms and misses read ~6-8ms, so with a near-even split the median lands on the seam and one sample swings it several ms. That is why the range below is 0.9-6.3 for a metric whose first recorded value was 1.1. Judge a breach by the ceiling, never by distance from these.

firstPaint.note: COLD first paint (2026-08-11, headless Chromium, NO throttle, 7 fresh contexts per run). Four runs: three standalone and one through the real nightly selection (`--grep @perf --workers=2 --retries=1`, after the three throttled render tests). p50 by run: 1286, 1298, 1345 standalone, 1322 full-tier - the full-tier run sits INSIDE the standalone spread, so co-locating this test with the throttled ones costs nothing measurable. That is the evidence for keeping all @perf tests in ONE serial file: a second @perf FILE would run beside this one at workers:2 and both measurements would degrade.

regressionScale.note: The regression these exist to catch, for scale. Before #1280 the gallery deck re-parsed the WHOLE deck on every keystroke because the progress rail and watermark glyph derived their section by walking every section.

ceilings.note: Chosen against the WORST observed value, not the best, and against the regression actually worth catching. Gallery typing was 63.2ms RENDER p50 before #1280 - a 30ms ceiling still catches that at half its magnitude while sitting 5.7x above the worst healthy reading. An earlier cut set navigation at 15/45, which left only 2.2x over a healthy gallery TOTAL of 20.6ms - too thin against this infrastructure's admitted 2x session-to-session drift, i.e. a false alarm waiting for a slow runner. ONE HONEST LIMIT: totalP50 70 sits only 5.7% above the 74.2ms pre-#1280 TOTAL this file records as its reason to exist, so on a runner ~6% faster the TOTAL ceiling would miss that regression entirely. RENDER is what actually catches it (30 vs 63.2, a 2.1x margin); treat TOTAL as a secondary backstop for regressions that bypass the engine, not as a second line of defense on the same one.

firstPaint.note: COLD BOOT, a different shape from the two above: one elapsed span, so one number. The span is the page's own performance.now() at paint - i.e. FROM NAVIGATION START, so it includes connect, HTML, parse and every blocking/deferred script, then hydrate, chunk load and render. That is deliberate and was NOT true of the first cut, which timed wall-clock inside the fixture and therefore began after `goto(..., 'domcontentloaded')` resolved: a 2s render-blocking script took real boot 1.1s -> 3.2s and moved the number by nothing. Fixed and demonstrated (1293ms -> 3150ms for the same injected 2s delay). 6000 is ~4.5x the worst healthy p50 measured (1345ms) and ~3.4x the worst SINGLE sample (1789ms). THREE HONEST LIMITS. (1) Provisional against the machine that matters: every reading is a 4-core sandbox and no GitHub runner has ever run this ceiling, so the headroom is sized for a runner-speed unknown rather than for observed variance - which is tight (1154-1789ms across 28 samples in 4 runs). The @perf log prints the p50 every night; tighten this once real runs are on record. (2) A single paint slower than the fixture's FIRST_PAINT_TIMEOUT (45s) fails inside `waitForStudioPaint` with its own tokenless error, so a boot regression past ~33x is filed as a harness failure rather than a breach. The test slot itself is no longer the binding constraint (it is sized at SAMPLES x FIRST_PAINT_TIMEOUT), but this residual remains. (3) It guards the DESKTOP project only, because perf-nightly.yml's @perf step runs --project=desktop; boot on a phone, where it is felt most, is still unguarded. NOT A LIMIT BUT A USAGE NOTE: this ceiling assumes the low concurrency the nightly runs. `npm run test:e2e -- --workers=8` puts cold paint near 9s on a 4-core box and would false-alarm it - the same contention sensitivity the two interaction ceilings above have, and why studio-e2e-nightly.yml runs --grep-invert @perf.

emulator.note: NO SEPARATE RENDER HARNESS IS NEEDED - but the emulator is NOT fully covered, and an earlier version of this note said it was. lattice-emulator.js:1681 calls latticeEngine.createEngine() and :1691 calls engine.render(), so the P2 swap (2026-06-11-emulator-on-engine-p2.md) left it a wrapper with no render path of its own; `bench`'s render tier already times that code. What is NOT measured by anything is the rest of the CLI pipeline - inlineLogoMarkSvg's per-mark file reads, the per-section image-scrim pass, the mermaid-cli subprocess per diagram, the in-page overflow/legibility probes, the measured overflow split loop, font settle, page.pdf() and the pdf-lib assembly. Measured on examples/a11y.md: the full export is ~8s wall, of which engine.render is ~10ms - about 0.1%. `bench --export` does not touch it either (the rasterize tier drives its own srcdoc through Puppeteer and never loads lattice-emulator.js).
